chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, and Yunus ibn Yaqoub narrated, saying:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Ihram, 'From which part of the Aqeeq is it superior that I should enter the state of Ihram?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'From its beginning is superior.'

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْعَقِيقِ: A valley or specific geographical location

ai.seo_question: Where is the best place to enter Ihram when performing Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the preferred Miqat by specifying that entering Ihram from the beginning of the Aqeeq is superior, reflecting the scholarly principle of prioritizing the initial point of the designated boundary for spiritual readiness. This guidance underscores the importance of adhering to specific geographical markers during Hajj, a practice rooted in the Prophet’s tradition and elaborated upon by Shia jurists to ensure ritual validity and excellence (Istihbab).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Ihraam, ‘From where in Al-Aqeeq is it superior that I should wear Ihraam?’ So heasws said: ‘From its beginning, is superior’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-‘Aqiq and which part of it is more virtuous for assuming the state of Ihram. He (the Imam) said, ‘Its beginning is better for assuming the state of Hiram.’”
